title: Serving and how guests order
lead: The words guests use at the bar, and how to take a drink order right the first time.

sections.name: Neat, up and on the rocks

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Three words tell you how a spirit is served.

know: Neat is the spirit alone in the glass: no ice, nothing added.
On The Rocks means poured over ice.
Up is chilled with ice, then strained into a glass with no ice.
Straight Up is unclear: some guests mean up, some mean neat. Ask.

sections.name: Well, call and premium

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Naming a brand changes the drink and the price.

know: Well is the house pour when a guest doesn’t name a brand.
Call is when the guest names the brand they want.
Premium is the top shelf: the bottles that cost the most.
Repeat It back so the guest gets, and pays for, what they asked for.

sections.name: Dry, dirty and with a twist

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Martini orders have their own words.

know: Dry means less vermouth; wet means more.
Dirty means olive brine goes in the drink.
Twist is a strip of citrus peel, its oils squeezed over the drink.
Gibson is a martini garnished with a cocktail onion.
Perfect means equal parts sweet and dry vermouth.

sections.name: Taking the order

lines.label: In short
lines.text: A clear order is the first step of a good drink.

know: Spirit first: which spirit, then which brand.
How they like it: neat, on the rocks or up.
Allergies matter at the bar too: egg white, nuts, dairy.
Repeat the order back before it goes in.
21 and over: check ID the way the Safety page says.

read.bigIdea: Three words tell you how a spirit is served.
read.where: **Neat** is the spirit alone, with no ice. **On the rocks** is over ice. **Up** means shaken or stirred with ice, then strained into a stemmed glass with no ice.
read.mixup: **Neat** never touches ice. **Up** is chilled on ice, but the ice stays in the tin.
read.sayIt: Would you like that neat or on the rocks?

read.bigIdea: Naming a brand changes the drink and the price.
read.where: A guest who orders a “vodka soda” gets the **well** vodka, the house pour. “Tito’s and soda” names the brand, so it’s a **call** drink. **Premium** bottles are the top shelf and cost more. The Back Bar shows which bottles sit in each tier.
read.sayIt: Any vodka you like, or our house vodka?

read.bigIdea: Martini orders have their own words.
read.where: **Dry** means less vermouth; **wet** means more. **Dirty** adds olive brine. A **twist** is a strip of lemon peel squeezed over the glass so its oils land on the drink. A **Gibson** is a martini with a cocktail onion. A **perfect** Manhattan uses equal parts sweet and dry vermouth.
read.mixup: Olives make it a martini with olives. **Brine** in the drink makes it **dirty**.
read.sayIt: Gin or vodka? And olives or a twist?

facts.fact: Neat is the spirit alone, with no ice. On the rocks is over ice. Up means shaken or stirred with ice, then strained into a stemmed glass with no ice.

A guest who orders a “vodka soda” gets the well vodka, the house pour. “Tito’s and soda” names the brand, so it’s a call drink. Premium bottles are the top shelf and cost more. The Back Bar shows which bottles sit in each tier.

Dry means less vermouth; wet means more. Dirty adds olive brine. A twist is a strip of lemon peel squeezed over the glass so its oils land on the drink. A Gibson is a martini with a cocktail onion. A perfect Manhattan uses equal parts sweet and dry vermouth.

Get the spirit, the brand and how they like it. Ask about allergies: some cocktails use egg white, nut syrups such as orgeat (made from almonds), or cream. Repeat the order back before it goes in. We serve guests 21 and over.
